reason: Source and named-import ordering port exactly with the M5 compare: an import fails when its module path sorts before the path of the import directly before it (through comments; another statement ends the block) after the option's transform (fold-upper for case-insensitive, fold-lower for -legacy, lowercase-first), relative paths sorting last as compare() does; named imports report the first specifier followed by a smaller one. What remains is TSLint's blank-line block boundary, invisible to relations: every import after a blank line that sorts before the one above is a false positive (36 FP). grouped-imports/groups check the order of those blank-line blocks, and module-source-path basename compares only the text after the last slash, which compare has no transform for; neither is ported.

evidence.why: `'abc'` follows `'foo'` across a blank line. TSLint starts a new block there, but the blank line is not visible to follows, so the port reports a false positive
'app_a/foo' after 'app_b/...' is found by comparing the full paths (was a first-character enumeration)
basename ordering compares the text after the last '/', which the port does not transform
